title: ECTODERMAL DYSPLASIA 17 WITH OR WITHOUT LIMB MALFORMATIONS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the LEF1 gene on chromosome 4q25.

checks.claim: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the LEF1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We provide further evidence for LEF1 haploinsufficiency role in ectodermal dysplasia and delineate its clinical phenotype.
checks.explanation: The paper supports a heterozygous change (deletion leading to haploinsufficiency) causing ectodermal dysplasia. It does not address homozygous mutations or point mutations.

checks.claim: The LEF1 gene is located on chromosome 4q25.
checks.evidence_quote: We report two unrelated patients with 4q25 de novo deletion encompassing LEF1
checks.explanation: The 4q25 deletion includes LEF1, which places the gene at 4q25.

paragraphs.text: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is a disorder in which ectodermal dysplasia occurs with or without limb malformations. Ectodermal features include severe oligodontia of the primary and permanent teeth, hypotrichosis, and hypohidrosis (Lévy et al., 2020). Limb malformations include radial ray defects, polydactyly, and split hand/foot. Depending on the type and location of the LEF1 variant, the disorder can be inherited in an autosomal dominant or an autosomal recessive pattern (Dufour et al., 2022).

paragraphs.text: Dufour et al. (2022) reported 12 individuals with LEF1 variants: 11 affected individuals from 4 unrelated families and 1 affected individual from a consanguineous family. The phenotypic spectrum included ectodermal dysplasia and various limb malformations, such as radial ray defects, polydactyly, and split hand/foot.

paragraphs.text: Using high-throughput sequencing, Dufour et al. (2022) found monoallelic LEF1 variants in 11 affected individuals from 4 unrelated families with ECTD17. They found a biallelic LEF1 variant in an affected individual from a consanguineous family. The authors studied the cellular consequences using immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, pulldown assays, and/or RNA sequencing. The functional data pointed to 2 molecular mechanisms. Haploinsufficiency or loss of DNA binding was associated with a mild to moderate phenotype. Loss of beta-catenin binding caused by biallelic variants was associated with a severe phenotype. Transcriptomic studies showed altered WNT signaling.
